newsitem.title: UK: UK business group says worried at cost of tax cut.
newsitem.headline: UK business group says worried at cost of tax cut.

text.p: The British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) said it was worried at the potential cost in the form of higher interest rates that could result from Britain's one percentage point cut in the basic rate of tax on Tuesday.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said in his 1997/98 budget speech on Tuesday he would cut the basic rate of tax by one penny per pound to 23 pence.

"The worry for business is that while the cut is affordable to the Exchequer, it may not be affordable to business if interest rates have to rise," said BCC President David Richardson in a statement after the budget speech.
"A penny cut in income tax will do nothing for business and investment. Only time will be the test of the inflationary consequences of this one penny cut."
Richardson said businesses would have preferred any changes in income tax to be restricted to the thresholds.
He added, "As for the abolition of tax relief on profit related pay, it will cost business to fund the difference, which itself will prove inflationary."
